recent.quoted_text: Henrik + Daniel Sedin briefing the media 1/4 way through the #Canucks season. They're opening their statement by suggesting that this availability reflects their commitment to transparency. "We took this job because we were tired of being mediocre," Henrik says of rebuilding.

recent.text: overarching takeaways from Sedins is that they don’t like the #Canucks current state of affairs, but they were prepared for pain. They think this roster is capable of more than it has shown to this point, but also understand this is life at start of a rebuild

recent.text: "We're not going to trade away players just to get more draft picks," said Henrik Sedin. "You also need to put a better product on the ice." #Canucks "Draft picks alone isn't going to get us through this," adds Daniel later on.
recent.author: Thomas Drance

recent.text: Henrik Sedin went on to talk about how you can’t just trade all your veterans for picks. That they still feel an obligation to support their young players with veterans. #Canucks
recent.author: Brendan Batchelor
recent.quoted_text: Henrik Sedin: You can’t just add picks. You have to build your team with players as well…we’re looking daily at improving our team. #Canucks

recent.text: "There's no real timeline," said Henrik Sedin on the topic of Thatcher Demko. "He's here, he's rehabbing, he's in a good mood and he's getting better." #Canucks

recent.text: Henrik Sedin talks about how it’s common for young players to enter the league on bad teams as part of rebuilds in the modern NHL, but it’s about how you handle that adversity that counts. #Canucks

recent.text: Daniel Sedin: Our belief is that our players are going to look at every day as an opportunity to get better so that you don’t end up in this situation again. #Canucks

recent.text: #Canucks Sedin on the fans: "People are knowledgeable, fans are knowledgeable. They know when guys are putting in the effort and they respect that. And that's what we need to see every night on the ice."
